The quantum-inspired nature of these algorithms makes them mappable to parametrized quantum circuits (PQCs), which is now fueling proposals for leveraging near-term quantum devices to enhance algorithm performance. Furthermore, joint quantum-classical frameworks can exploit the unique strengths of TNs and PQC models. Nonetheless, approximating TN states using realistic quantum circuits remains a pending issue for the success of such approaches. Our study assesses novel and existing protocols for decomposing matrix product states into shallow quantum circuits consisting of stacked linear layers of two-qubit gates, incorporating both analytical decomposition schemes and constrained optimization of circuit unitaries. Our experiments demonstrate the superiority of a sequential growth protocol, especially when computational resources are limited, leading us to anticipate that this protocol will become a crucial tool for integrating tensor networks and quantum circuits.

Automated cell identification and differentiation have been heavily relied upon by medical professionals, leading to increased importance attached to this task.  A key factor in achieving accurate cell identification and differentiation is the use of high-quality datasets with annotated markers and appropriate algorithms.  However, existing datasets are limited by their size, the marker annotation, and the performance of methods used for extraction and identification.  To address these challenges, this study presents a novel, large-scale dataset comprising over 150,000 annotated cells across four cancer types using flow cytometry.  The dataset uses a unique data curation process to ensure high quality and diversity.  Furthermore, the study introduces a new deep learning architecture called MultiCon-ResNet to solve the multi-channel multi-classification task.  The method achieves exceptional accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art models with an average accuracy of 99.72% and a macro average accuracy of 97.68%.  To demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, it is applied to cancer identification and sub-type classification using the new dataset as well as other publicly available datasets. Combining these detections with electromagnetic radiation holds significant potential to improve our comprehension of neutron star events, particularly their dense matter state. However, electromagnetic analysis of gravitational waves necessitates the use of multi-messenger templates that incorporate equation of state effects. We have utilized the 4th-order resummation template to analyze the open-field dynamical simulation of a neutron star merger that resulted in a short gamma-ray burst. We have found that this template effectively recovers key parameters of the merger, including the mass ratio, spin, and orientation of any electromagnetic emission. We have also investigated the impact of higher-order modes and found that they contribute substantially to the signal for mass ratios above 1. If detected in actual data, a short gamma-ray burst associated with a mass ratio greater than 1 could offer strong evidence in favor of black hole formation.

, has historically been challenging for object-oriented programming due to inefficiencies in memory allocation and access.  Despite this limitation, a range of applications, including real-world programs with inherent object structures, have been overlooked for parallelization opportunities.  Our research identified a particular subset of object-oriented programming called Single-Method Multiple-Objects (SMMO), which can be efficiently parallelized on SIMD devices by executing the same method across multiple objects of a given type.  To facilitate easy adoption of high-speed GPU programming for average developers, we created the DynaSOAr CUDA framework specifically tailored for SMMO applications.  This framework includes a dynamic memory allocator that is both lock-free and parallel, a data layout domain-specific language (DSL), and a do-all operation that is both parallel and efficient.  As a result, DynaSOAr offers improved global memory access rates, reduced memory allocation times, and overall faster execution times compared to standard GPU programming methods, leading to up to $30\times$ performance boosts for real-world applications.

A new regularization method has been proposed to take advantage of O(1) optically thick cores, potentially significantly speeding up cloud tomography. This method could be useful for initial studies and future applications with limited amounts of spectrally multiplexed data.

X-ray emission line mapping, essential for studying ICM turbulence, is complicated by the lack of high-resolution spectroscopy. Future X-ray detectors like the X-IFU on Athena will enable thorough investigations of ICM turbulence across multiple scales. Crucial to these studies is the accurate estimation of turbulent velocities and lengths, which involve estimating non-thermal broadening of emission lines. Here, an alternative method for calculating turbulent lengths is proposed, based on the ratio of turbulent to thermal pressures. This approach, unlike previous line-ratio methods that require turbulent velocities and lengths, allows for direct measurement of turbulent lengths. Both analytical and numerical models demonstrate that this ratio can be resolved and reconstructed at reasonable signal-to-noise rates, leading to feasible measurements of turbulent lengths in galaxy clusters. This is achievable even with lower-resolution detectors, as long as they can resolve the width of the central peak of a line profile resulting from turbulent broadening.

Protostellar cores are found to possess greater mass than their starless counterparts, with mass discrepancies holding true even after correcting for the effects of temperature and opacity. This study explores algebraic and relational semantics for Godel modal logics built upon the duality between finite Godel algebras and finite forests, a type of poset. The research considers subvarieties of basic Godel algebras with two modal operators, alongside their respective classes of forest frames, both with single and double accessibility relations. These relational structures serve as prelinear counterparts to traditional intuitionistic modal logic semantics. The study specifically examines two expansions of finite Godel algebras: the addition of Dunn axioms, common in positive classical and intutionistic logic, and the addition of Fischer Servi axioms. The research provides Jonsson-Tarski-like representation theorems for different types of finite Godel modal algebras with operators.

Typically, this issue arises when dealing with non-interacting particles in an ideal gas during free expansion, where standard equilibrium thermodynamics fails to provide a description of the system's state when the volume changes. We've, however, utilized the nonequilibrium distribution of phase microstates to develop a non-equilibrium entropy function that depends on both the system's macrostate and its specific microstate. This model has the ability to smoothly transition between the equations of state for dark energy and dust at different cosmological epochs, by asymptotically interpolating between two power laws. A constant viscosity coefficient underlies the model's dissipative component. Using a phase space analysis, we investigate the model's dynamics in a framework that is robust and solution-independent. Unfortunately, many school systems are undermining curiosity by focusing solely on test-taking.  However, educators are seeking ways to design curriculum and instruction that not only meets academic standards but also fosters curiosity.  This study introduces a design framework called TEST that guides curriculum and instruction design to foster curiosity.  The proposed framework is based on three interconnected concepts: triggering questions that spark curiosity, escalating tests that both satisfy curiosity and deepen understanding, emotional safety that fosters curiosity expression, and collaborative learning that satisfies curiosity and builds community.  The framework integrates triggering questions, escalating tests, and emotional safety to create space for curiosity expression, and then integrates collaborative learning to facilitate curiosity satisfaction.  The framework is illustrated with examples from various subjects and grade levels, and the study offers research questions for further exploration.

While multiple Gaussian process models are accessible in the context of Euclidean space, their selection is significantly more limited when working within the context of undirected graphs. This research adapts the stochastic partial differential equation formulation for Mat\'ern Gaussian processes to improve standard Gaussian process models and present them within the context of undirected graphs. A new Gaussian process model, named Graph Mat\'ern Gaussian processes, is introduced using this formulation. The model employs a heavy-tailed prior in the form of an undirected factor graph, which is computationally efficient to factorize. It is particularly useful for learning the hyperparameters of the model in a manner consistent with maximum a posteriori estimation through the use of intimated variational inference. For more intricate datasets that include both node and edge information, a joint model is also proposed in order to utilize this additional form of side information.

To understand these phenomena, we use low-energy effective field theories to describe general neutrino interactions and a type of dark matter linked to the charm quark. Moreover, our analysis revealed that J/ψ invisible decays can be sensitive to light dark matter mass ranges inaccessible to direct detection experiments, with future facilities such as the Super Tau Charm Factory having the potential to significantly lower these limits by two orders of magnitude.

AR at the Max-Planck Institute for Plasma Physics in Germany is designed to investigate how plasma interacts with radio frequency waves. A plasma source with a 0.1 meter length and 0.4 meter diameter provides plasma necessary for the experiment, and features a helical antenna to produce high-density plasma in the helicon mode of discharge. Until now, it was unclear if this plasma source could achieve helicon mode, which is essential for it to function effectively. A study was conducted to verify this capability, involving detailed analysis of plasma parameters and particle power balance using a global model. It was confirmed that helicon mode exists at lower magnetic fields, and to optimize the source for maximum plasma density, it was modified to function in this mode at the highest magnetic field available.

cancer diagnosis, it requires significant effort to perform tasks like identifying and counting individual cells. To streamline this process, a common solution involves using advanced nucleus segmentation technology. Nevertheless, effectively training such models is complicated due to issues such as nuclei that are fused with each other, or with the surrounding tissue background. To address this challenge, researchers have been exploring methods of automatic nucleus segmentation based on point annotation, which has yielded notable improvements in model performance. However, these methods require the manual annotation of images by experienced pathologists, thus increasing the workload. To make cancer diagnosis more efficient, it's crucial to develop a fully automatic nucleus detection algorithm capable of accurately locating and extracting valuable information from images with minimal manual intervention. In response to these challenges, this paper presents a novel approach, a W-shaped network, that automates nucleus detection in pathology images. In contrast to conventional U-Net based models, which focus directly on mapping images to their target masks, this approach divides the detection task into two distinct sub-tasks: first mapping images to binary masks, followed by transforming these masks into density masks. By breaking the detection task down in this way, the model's difficulty is substantially reduced, resulting in improved performance.

Pyroptosis is primarily initiated through the NLRP3 inflammasome's formation and can be triggered by cell damage, viral infections, and other stimuli. The current study investigates the impact of the NLRP3 inflammasome on the severity of SARS-CoV-2 infection using the SARS-CoV-2 virus, remdesivir, fake remdesivir, NLRP3 activators and inhibitors in A549 cells, as well as clinical data from COVID-19 patients. The findings show that NLRP3 activation leads to pyroptotic cell death, high IL-1β levels, and cell damage caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Remdesivir and NLRP3 inhibitors can slow down cell death and reduce IL-1β production. NLRP3 activation levels were correlated with IL-1β concentrations and disease severity in SARS-CoV-2 patients. The findings confirm that NLRP3 activation plays a crucial role in SARS-CoV-2-induced pyroptosis, cell death, and inflammation, and that remdesivir and NLRP3 inhibitors may be potential treatments for SARS-CoV-2-induced pyroptosis, inflammation, and associated organ failure.

This concept of retrospectively discounted reinforcement mathematically formalizes the relationship between the reward stream and an internally generated state sequence, thereby establishing a Markov property. a particular n-tuple $(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ within the range [0,1] is classified as 'cyclic' when there exist unique, independent random variables $(U_1, \ldots, U_n)$ where the probability of each variable being less than or equal to $x_i$ exceeds 0.5, yet the combined condition of all variables simultaneously meeting this threshold results in a combined probability less than 1 divided by n. Our primary finding, based on the concept of probability, allows us to calculate the maximum possible value for n, which is 3, indicating that all-cyclic tuples are impossible to occur in any scenario involving four or more dimensions. Notably, this discovery led us to uncover a new class of geometric shapes known as 'cyclic slices,' which are specific regions within an n-dimensional cube. These regions correspond to the probability space defined by the variables $(U_1, \ldots, U_n)$. Our research also included an exploration of the boundaries defining these shapes in 4-dimensional space, as well as the identification of areas where the minimum joint probability can be found.

Traditionally, THz communication is confined to short-distance applications because THz signals face high absorption in the atmosphere. To overcome this limitation, researchers have explored the potential of multi-hop directional transmission techniques to extend communication range, albeit these schemes can result in prolonged beam training time using conventional methods such as exhaustive search or hierarchical approaches. This method's efficiency is optimal for high-frequency scenarios and is adaptable across any given frequency $\omega$. The approach operates within a time-domain framework, consisting of three main components: generating a suitable incoming plane wave with compact propagation direction, solving the time-domain scattering problem, and ultimately deriving the time-harmonic solution via Fourier transformation. In contrast to the water-rich Antarctic samples with terrestrial contamination, Benenitra and Chelyabinsk pyroxene minerals showed lower levels of water (around 0.018-0.087 wt.$\%$ H$_2$O) and D-poor isotopic signatures, ranging from -444 to -49. Evaluating various processes on small parent bodies, our analysis suggested minimal water loss during thermal metamorphism, and the water content in Benenitra and Chelyabinsk pyroxene minerals can be explained by a mixture of D-poor nebular hydrogen and D-rich water from mesostases. Approximately 45-95$\%$ of water with low D isotope values in the pyroxene minerals came from nebular hydrogen, and it's possible that S-type asteroids with nominally anhydrous minerals can hold significant amounts of water (254-518 ppm). This finding may imply a reduced need for additional volatile delivery to the terrestrial planets during the final stages of planetary accretion, given the water added to the nominally dry inner Solar System bodies during the accretion process.

We aim to build zero-shot speech-to-text models that learn speech recognition and machine translation but can execute the speech-to-text task. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. By incorporating an encoder from the Cyclic Reverse Generator framework, we successfully developed an inverse mapping system to recreate synthetic X-rays accurately and reconstruct organs on real X-rays. By fine-tuning latent codes, we successfully transplanted a cardiac enlargement condition onto normal chest X-rays. Our research was showcased at the Medical Imaging meets NeurIPS Workshop 2020, a satellite event of the 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems held in Vancouver, Canada.

For domains with irregular boundaries, using a grid without a set pattern to calculate the potential by splitting it into small areas becomes impractical due to high computational costs. In this paper, we propose an efficient and straightforward high-order method for calculating Newtonian potentials based on Green's identity, which simplifies the complex volume integration into boundary integrals. These boundary integrals can then be computed quickly using the Helsing-Ojala method. Our new method makes expensive computations of near field interactions on an unstructured grid comparable to the time it takes for far field interactions. An essential component of our method involves using a high-order approximation to represent a function over a grid cell, which traditionally poses an ill-conditioned problem due to solving a system of equations involving Vandermonde matrices. Notably, smooth functions and a backward-stable solver for linear systems allow this approximation to be accurate over a grid cell when done correctly. In this paper, we provide a precise proof of this concept. We demonstrate our algorithm's effectiveness through several numerical experiments.
